candidates.attacker_control: A remote HTTP client controls the request path of any GET that matches a registered asset route (AssetCompiler.patterns() produces routes such as '/css/**' and '/js/**' from configured filesets). It can supply encoded traversal segments (e.g. '/css/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd', or double-encoded '%252e%252e' against servlet/undertow) which Jooby decodes before asset resolution.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The parent AssetHandler.loader() normalizes and verifies path.startsWith(basedir) before returning a URL (AssetHandler.java:567-582) - but that code is bypassed because FileSystemAssetHandler overrides resolve(String), not loader(). Prod packaging disables watch (jooby-maven-plugin AssetMojo.java:306-308 and jooby-gradle-plugin AssetTask.java:352-354 write 'assets.watch = false' into dist configs), so the exposure is mainly dev/staging unless watch is enabled elsewhere; the Jooby default application.host may be loopback, limiting remote exposure. Jetty rejects single-encoded dot segments as ambiguous, but the double-decoding in ServletServletRequest means a double-encoded '%252e%252e' passes container validation and is decoded to '..' by Router.decode; Netty does not normalize at all. No other path-confinement/validation filter for asset requests was found in the snapshot. Files.exists() does not canonicalize and therefore cannot substitute for the missing check.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary read of files readable by the server process (application source, configuration/secrets, other users' files) via a normal GET to an asset route; information disclosure that can directly enable further compromise (credentials, keys, environment files). Responses are served as assets, so response size/media type follow the target file.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses the jooby-assets module; assets watch/live-compiler mode is active (default in dev per doc/doc/assets/assets.md and Assets.configure:517, and settable via assets.watch anywhere); at least one asset pattern is registered and matches the request; the target file is readable by the JVM process; the dev/watched server is reachable from the attacker (default host may be loopback, but dev servers are routinely exposed on 0.0.0.0/containers).
candidates.root_cause: FileSystemAssetHandler.resolve(String) joins the request-derived asset path onto configured roots with Path.resolve() and only tests Files.exists(), without normalize()/startsWith(root) confinement. The parent AssetHandler.loader() performs exactly that check (normalize + startsWith(basedir)) before returning a resource, but the assets subclass overrides resolve() and drops the confinement for the watch/live-compiler mode. Because the asset path is built from the decoded HTTP path (HttpHandlerImpl normalizes only the trailing slash; NettyRequest/UndertowRequest/ServletServletRequest call Router.decode, which URL-decodes the path, and servlet/undertow input is already container-decoded), '%2e%2e'/'%2f' sequences become '..'/'' and escape the configured roots. URLAsset then opens the resulting file (FileInputStream) and the framework serves it.
candidates.title: Path traversal in jooby-assets watched asset handler (FileSystemAssetHandler) allows arbitrary file read
candidates.trace: Observed source path: (1) Assets.configure selects the watch branch when watch=true and constructs new FileSystemAssetHandler("/", workdir, publicDir) (Assets.java:517-523); (2) routes are registered for configured asset patterns, e.g. '/css/**' (Assets.java:566; AssetCompiler.patterns() javadoc, lines 340-359); (3) AssetHandler.handle() takes req.path() and calls resolve(req, path) (AssetHandler.java:458-460); (4) init() sets fn = p -> p.substring(1) for pattern '/', so the target is the decoded request path without its leading slash (AssetHandler.java:554-560); (5) dynamic dispatch reaches FileSystemAssetHandler.resolve(), which does source.resolve(path).filter(Files::exists) with no normalize/containment (FileSystemAssetHandler.java:224-231) - e.g. workdir.resolve("css/../../../etc/passwd") exists; (6) the resulting file URL is wrapped in URLAsset, whose attr() opens a FileInputStream for local files (URLAsset.java:288-296), and the file content is sent. Encoding gate: HttpHandlerImpl.normalizeURI only strips a trailing slash (HttpHandlerImpl.java:604-607) and Router.decode() applies URLDecoder.decode to the path (Router.java:234-236); NettyRequest decodes query.path() once (NettyRequest.java:289-294) while ServletServletRequest/UndertowRequest decode an already container-decoded path a second time (ServletServletRequest.java:251-255, UndertowRequest.java:256-261), so '%252e%252e' survives container normalization and becomes '..' for Jooby.
candidates.unverified: assets.conf (which defines the actual fileset/route patterns) and all test sources are absent from this snapshot, so the exact registered patterns could not be read (AssetCompiler.patterns() documentation and usage imply '/css/**', '/js/**'); no code was executed, so the end-to-end request could not be confirmed at runtime and server-specific path handling is argued from source, not observed. Whether the ground-truth exposure is considered dev-only in the project's security model is unknown.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 4,849 readable files, 5 MiB per-file text limit, no binary/sensitive-name/symlink exclusions; get_relation_scope: 904 files indexed, 493 Java files parsed, 7 omitted, 1 parse error, index status 'partial' with no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution. I inspected the core framework (handlers/AssetHandler, Cors/CorsHandler, CsrfHandler, SSIHandler, HttpHandlerImpl, Request/Response implementations, routing/RoutePattern, sessions and cookie/session managers, MediaType, Err/error rendering, FlashScope) and the security-relevant modules (jooby-assets including FileSystemAssetHandler/AssetCompiler/LiveCompiler/AssetVars, jooby-apitool, jooby-crash, jooby-pac4j and jooby-pac4j2, jooby-metrics, jooby-whoops, jooby-livereload, and the netty/servlet/undertow/jetty backends). No test sources and no .conf files exist in the snapshot; third-party webjar contents are absent. Uninspected areas include most data-store/ORM/template/asset-processor modules (e.g. jdbc/jdbi/jooq/ebean/mongodb/cassandra/neo4j, ftl/hbs/pebble/thymeleaf/jade/rocker, asset processors) and build tooling, which were only spot-checked via text search.
limitations: No runtime execution, dependency resolution, or HTTP testing was performed; reachability arguments are source-based (index explicitly lacks data flow and reachability).

assets.conf and test sources are not part of the snapshot, so the exact asset route patterns and expected behavior could not be read directly; module docs and code indicate patterns such as /css/** and /js/**.
Server-specific URI handling (Jetty rejection of encoded dot segments, Undertow normalization) is argued from the request classes in this snapshot, not observed.
The candidate is exposed in watch/live-compiler mode, which is enabled by default only in dev and explicitly disabled in generated dist configs; production exposure requires assets.watch=true.
The exact upstream fix history/CVE mapping for this snapshot could not be consulted (no web, no repository history in the snapshot).

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS via the 'theme' query parameter in jooby-apitool (ApiTool.java:1035-1041 RAML and 1093-1100 Swagger): req.param("theme") is concatenated into the HTML page returned with MediaType.html with no escaping.
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control and unescaped HTML concatenation are visible in source, but the injection only occurs if the external webjar index pages (api-console 3.0.17 / swagger-ui 3.17.1) actually contain the replace anchors ('api-console-light-theme.css', '<style>'); those artifacts are not in the snapshot, so exploitability could not be verified. Kept as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated CRaSH web shell: WebShellHandler.onOpen (modules/jooby-crash/.../WebShellHandler.java:233-269) and HttpShellPlugin (lines 225-241) call ShellFactory.create(null) and execute client-supplied commands with no authentication or environment guard.
rejected_leads.reason: High impact (remote command execution) but the module is an explicitly opt-in developer tool whose documentation advertises the shell; it additionally requires an extra connector artifact (crash.connectors.web or explicit plugin registration). Documented/opt-in behavior made this a rejected rather than selected lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Java deserialization of session values via ObjectInputStream.readObject in modules/jooby-pac4j (AuthSerializer.java:219-230) and modules/jooby-pac4j2 (Pac4jSessionStore.java:272-281).
rejected_leads.reason: The serialized values come from Jooby Session attributes, which are server-side (Mem/other stores) or, for cookie sessions, HMAC-signed and rejected when the signature does not verify (CookieSessionManager.attributes / Cookie.Signature.unsign). No path was found where an attacker can place serialized data into the session.

rejected_leads.lead: Non-constant-time comparison of HMAC/token values (Cookie.Signature.unsign uses mac.equals(value), Cookie.java:654-665; CsrfHandler token.equals(candidate), CsrfHandler.java:343).
rejected_leads.reason: Timing side channel / hardening issue only; practical MAC or CSRF-token recovery over a network was not substantiated from source evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: CORS handler reflects the request Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials when the default origin '*' is configured (CorsHandler.java:284-307, Cors.java:324-332).
rejected_leads.reason: Behavior is opt-in via installing CorsHandler and is configuration-dependent (origin/credentials values come from cors config not present in this snapshot); treated as a misconfiguration risk, not the strongest distinct vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Jooby URL-decodes paths with URLDecoder (Router.decode, Router.java:234-236) in servers that already decoded them (ServletServletRequest.java:255, UndertowRequest.java:260), i.e. double decoding.
rejected_leads.reason: This is an enabling condition for the selected finding rather than a separate root cause, so it is not submitted as its own candidate (avoiding splitting one root cause).

summary: Snapshot is Jooby 1.6.4-SNAPSHOT (mid-2019; Jetty 9.4.19 / Netty 4.1.37). I reviewed core HTTP handling (routing, request/response, sessions/cookies, CSRF/CORS, error rendering, assets) and the security-relevant modules (assets, apitool, crash, pac4j/pac4j2, metrics, whoops, livereload, servlet/netty/undertow/jetty backends). The single strongest source-evidenced issue is a path-traversal/arbitrary-file-read in the jooby-assets live (watched) asset handler: the request-derived asset path is resolved against configured directories with no normalization or containment check, unlike its parent class, and the HTTP path is URL-decoded by Jooby (twice on servlet/undertow), so encoded dot-dot segments reach the resolver. Other plausible issues (ApiTool `theme` reflected XSS, unauthenticated CRaSH web shell, pac4j `readObject`, non-constant-time MAC comparison, CORS origin reflection) were examined but are weaker, dependency-gated, or not attacker-controllable on the evidence available; they are listed as rejected leads.
